chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who prays the voluntary prayer while sitting, and there is no excuse for him in travel or in residence. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray voluntary prayers sitting down when healthy?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that sitting for voluntary prayers is permissible even without a valid excuse (‘illah), distinguishing it from obligatory prayers where sitting without cause is generally disliked or invalidating. This ruling underscores the flexibility and ease (taysir) inherent in nafl worship, allowing believers to adapt their posture to comfort or devotion without compromising validity.
